description: LynkOmni tracking (owner request 9 November 2026): one register of everything that moves through steps and that someone waits on, and one engine that follows it from the event log (services/tracking.py, ts/src/tracking.ts, shared vectors contract/vectors/tracking.v1.json). Each kind names its public id type (core/ids.py), the payload field that identifies the record, its steps in order with the events that reach them, who may see it and where. Screens, messages and automations read this file; no screen lists its own steps.
rules: A step is reached only by an event in the log (or, for services that keep their own state, by that service's state). Nothing is shown as done before the event that proves it: a delivery is delivered only on DeliveryDelivered, a payment confirmed only on the provider's callback.
The chip beside a tracker uses only the five states: queued, sent, accepted, confirmed, failed. The step word says what happened.

Screens show the steps reached so far, then the steps still expected; optional steps (a payment waiting for its provider, a repair waiting for parts) appear only once reached, and only one ending is shown: the one reached, or the one expected (a delivery when the order has one).
Customers see a tracker with no account at its public address and see only customer steps: never an address, a phone number, a name other than the shop's, a rider's identity or coordinates.

Live progress (delivery only) is a share between 0 and 1 and a time of arrival, worked out on LynkOmni's servers from positions the partner reports or the shop's own rider shares with consent during the trip. Positions are never stored in the event log, never shown to the customer, and are deleted when the trip ends.
A tracker is late when its promised time has passed and it has not ended; the owner is told (automation tracking-late-watch) and the customer sees the new estimate, never a guess.
Every step change a customer can see may send one message by the way they chose (automation order-updates: transactional, quiet hours, their language).

A step counts once. A step marked "again" can be reached again when its event comes again (a queue ticket waits again after Put back or Send to, and is called again); the current step is always the last one reached.

kinds.note: A LynkQueue ticket: waiting (also after Put back or Send to), called to a counter, done; missed, left or not served today. The place in the queue is a plain number on the ticket itself; customers see only these steps, never a name (NEW UPDATE 4; build section 3B).

One attendance record from check-in to check-out and any correction. A correction always has its reason and keeps the old line beside the new one; the person sees their own record only (TRACKING UPDATE 72.9; build section 3B).

A reward for a full answer, paid by the licensed payment partner from the organisation's own money: requested, then paid or not completed. Only the partner's answer, in the cloud, says it was paid; LynkOmni never holds a reward (TRACKING UPDATE 72.9; build section 3B).

An emulator offered to a device (QR code, Lynk Code or link, or one of the other ways): offered, accepted on the device, connected by the cloud; or denied. Staff and managers only (EMULATOR UPDATE; build section 3A).
An emulator moving to another device: the old device sends its unsent records first, then the emulator moves with its name, settings and printers (build section 3A).
A device not seen for a while waits for a manager to approve it again before it works (build section 3A).

A vote (LOVOT-) from set-up to published results (VOTE UPDATE 68; contract version 12). Voters see it open, close, counted and published. A ballot is never tracked or shown: the voter checks their own by its tracking code on the public list.

A signature request in LynkFiles (contract version 13): sent, signed by each signer in turn, completed or declined. Signers see it through their own signing link; no signer's name is shown to another.

An exchange order through the licensed partner (contract version 15): placed, paid to the partner, completed, or not completed and refunded. Only the partner's answers move it; a practice order says so. The person's own exchanges show on exchange.lynkomni.com, never on merchant screens.
A supplier's bill in LynkAcc: received, approved, partly paid, paid. Only a person approves; money moves only through the provider. Follows LynkAcc's own record (from_service_events).
A staff expense claim in LynkAcc: submitted, approved, repaid. Nobody approves their own claim; repaid only when the provider confirms.

One message from the message register: waiting to send (offline or quiet hours), sent through the channel the person chose, delivered in the app, or not completed on a channel. Never shows the message's words; a personal account tracker, never in an API.
A payments provider's payout to the shop's own bank or wallet (the payout calendar, 67.8): expected and arrived only from the provider; late is shown on the calendar, never claimed as lost.

A bet asked of the licensed operator (contract version 17). Online it is sent at once; offline it is a queued slip, never a ticket, only where the operator allows it. Only the operator's answers move it; a refused slip is refunded in full.
A big win referred to the operator's head office: referred, checking, approved, paid. Only the operator's answers move it; the winner sees the steps on their e-ticket.

A leave request in LynkHR (contract version 19): asked, then approved or declined by someone other than the person who asked, or cancelled. The person sees their own request at account.lynkomni.com/work.
A new staff member's joining in LynkHR: started, contract signed, ready once every must on the joining checklist is done.
A staff member's leaving in LynkHR: notice recorded, equipment back, access closed, left. Final pay figures go to LynkAcc only after the first three.
A review cycle in LynkHR: opened, answers coming in (peer and upward shown only from 3), signed off by a named manager.
A task in LynkProject: to do, in progress, waiting on another task, done or cancelled. A guest sees only the tasks of the project they were invited to.
A change request on a project: raised, then accepted or refused by a named person who did not raise it.
A project milestone: planned against its baseline, then reached.
A week's time sheet: sent for approval, then approved or returned by a manager, never the person who logged it. Approved billable time is billed once.
An approval route (bill, expense, invoice, document): waiting for each named approver in turn, approved or returned.
A request for a document (a staff file, a lease, a certificate): asked, received, checked.

planned.note: LynkSupport cases: received, in progress, waiting for you, resolved. Built with section 6 on the same engine.
Customer refunds through the licensed provider: requested, sent to provider, refunded or failed. Paid but undelivered purchases become refund_due.

LynkTrace shipments (NEW UPDATE 1): online shop orders, supplier purchase orders and parcels sent by own riders, partner carriers or agencies, with legs, scans, hand-overs, exceptions, attempts and receiver choices on the contract version 4 events. The receiver's tracking and custody pages come in section 7; the full engine in section 7B.
LynkBooking reservations and tickets: requested, confirmed by the provider, changed, used or refunded.
Airtime, data, bills and vouchers: paid, sent to provider, delivered or refund_due.
One leg of a journey (road, rail, sea or air) inside a shipment or a traveller's journey pass (LOTRP-).
A trip of a protected vehicle or asset (LynkGuard): started, in progress, ended, from AssetTripStarted and AssetTripEnded.
A rental from hand-over to return (LynkGuard rental mode): renter told, handed over, returned, checked.
A LynkSentry incident (LOSNT-): opened, with the owner and trusted contacts, closed; routed to the safety desk.
A verification by the licensed partner (LOVER-): sent, checked by the partner, confirmed or refused; only the partner's answer in the cloud confirms.
A change of plan: asked, takes effect at the date shown, nothing cut off mid-day.
A payment dispute, which opens a support case (LOCASE-): opened, evidence sent to the provider, won or lost.
A payment the provider holds until check-in or delivery: held, released or refunded.
A pre-order: placed, deposit confirmed by the provider, item arrived, collected or delivered.
A return of goods (LORFD-): asked, received, checked, refunded through the provider or exchanged.
A LynkVCard request to the licensed issuer: sent, checked, issued or refused; only the issuer's answer in the cloud confirms.
A traveller's journey (LOTRP-) made of bookings and legs: booked, checked in, on the way, arrived.
A job or property advert's review before it goes live: sent, checked, live or returned with a reason.
A tenancy deposit return through the deposit scheme or provider: asked, checked against the move-out photos, returned. LynkOmni never holds the deposit.
A report card: marks confirmed by the teachers, approved by the head, issued to guardians.
A developer app's review before it is listed on LynkHub: sent, checked, listed or returned.
A purchase order to a supplier: drafted from low stock, approved, sent, received, matched to the bill.
A stock transfer between branches: sent, on the way, received and counted.

from_service_events.rule: Services that keep their own state report it in their internal events; each line moves a tracker by feed_state (services/tracking.py PlatformTracking).

engine.agreed: Owner, 19 November 2026: TRACKING UPDATE (master blueprint section 72.3, 72.4 and 72.9); the section 4 engine upgrade
engine.at_risk_note: An item is at risk once it has spent 80% of its step's promised time in that step (basis points, 8000 = 80%), and late once it has spent all of it. Promised times are in minutes; a kind with working_time counts only the business's opening hours.
engine.stuck_note: An item is stuck when it has stayed in a step at least twice that step's promised time. It is listed and raised; nothing changes its step.
engine.keep_note: An ended tracker is kept this many days after its ending (a kind may say keep_days), then removed from the engine; the event log and the books keep their own keeping times.
engine.two_second_note: A step is visible within two seconds of its event: the engine applies a busy day's events and draws its views well inside that (tests/test_tracking_engine.py).
engine.late_events: An event that arrives late (an offline scan sent hours afterwards) lands in its true place: it never becomes the current step when a later step of the same flow was already reached at a later time. An event seen once (same event id) is never counted twice.
engine.clash: Two endings for one item (delivered on one device, failed on another, both offline) never overwrite each other: the ending with the earlier true time stands, the other is kept as a clash and raised to the owner to settle.
engine.flows: A kind's steps may be added to but never removed or renamed while items are on their way: every step id that ever existed stays (contract/vectors/tracking-steps.lock.json; tests/test_tracking_engine.py).
engine.extra_steps_note: A business may add up to five steps of its own to a kind (a quality check, a second count). They show on its own screens in time order, never change the five-state chip, never decide an ending and are shown to customers only when the business says so. Marked with TrackingStepMarked (contract version 18).
engine.practice: A tracker whose events carry practice true (practice mode) is never in the control tower's counts, the exception list, reports or messages.
engine.capacity: A promise from real capacity: base minutes plus whole rounds of the work already waiting (load divided by the people or machines on it, rounded up) times the minutes one round takes.
engine.partners: A partner's own status words never reach a screen: each is mapped here to the event LynkOmni's cloud writes for it; an unknown status is listed for staff and changes nothing.
engine.scan: A scan moves a step only where the register says (scan), only with the proof the step asks for, only after its checks pass, and only by an event a device may write; cloud-only steps are never scanned.
